etymologies.etymologyHTML: From dis- +‎ order. Middle English disordeine, from Old French desordainer, from Medieval Latin disordinare.

definitions.definition: Absence of order; state of not being arranged in an orderly manner.

quote.citation: 1986, John le Carré, A Perfect Spy:
quote.text: It was a household in permanent and benevolent  disorder, pervaded by the gentle thrill of religious persecution.

definitions.definition: A disturbance of civic peace or of public order.
(medicine, countable) A physical or mental malfunction.

quote.citation: 2015 December 21, Michael D. Geschwind, “Prion Diseases”, in Continuum (Minneap Minn), →DOI:
quote.text: A very rare polymorphism in the prion protein gene recently has been identified that appears to protect against prion disease; this finding, in addition to providing greater understanding of the prionlike mechanisms of neurodegenerative disorders, might lead to potential treatments.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To throw into a state of disorder.
(transitive) To knock out of order or sequence.
